note: Curated ingredient families (CAMP-style cross-reactor groups) and the purge-capable list. Every entry is a claim we can defend from the sources in docs/STRATEGY.md section 2. An exact ingredient match always ranks above a family match.

fragrance.label: fragrance and its declared components
fragrance.general_note: Fragrance components are among the most commonly reported contact irritants.

essential oils.label: essential oils
essential oils.general_note: Essential oils carry the same fragrance components in less predictable amounts.

drying alcohols.label: drying alcohols
drying alcohols.general_note: Short-chain alcohols evaporate fast and are often reported as stinging on dry or compromised skin. Fatty alcohols such as cetearyl alcohol are a different thing and are not in this family.

ahas.label: AHAs
ahas.general_note: AHAs exfoliate and speed up cell turnover.

bha.label: BHA
bha.general_note: Salicylic acid exfoliates inside the pore.

retinol.note: Retinoids speed up cell turnover, so purging is possible.

retinal.note: Retinoids speed up cell turnover, so purging is possible.

tretinoin.note: Retinoids speed up cell turnover, so purging is possible.

adapalene.note: Retinoids speed up cell turnover, so purging is possible.

glycolic acid.note: AHAs speed up cell turnover, so purging is possible.

lactic acid.note: AHAs speed up cell turnover, so purging is possible.

mandelic acid.note: AHAs speed up cell turnover, so purging is possible.

salicylic acid.note: Salicylic acid speeds up turnover inside the pore, so purging is possible.

azelaic acid.note: Azelaic acid can cause mild purging in some people, usually in the first 2-6 weeks.

gluconolactone.note: Gluconolactone is a mild PHA, so mild purging is possible.
